::: {.article-lede}
AI tools can make some tasks faster. The more interesting question is what happens to the quality of the work, the learning behind it, and our ability to judge the result.
:::

## Why I'm paying attention

Explain the question that motivates this series and what you hope to learn from observing your own work.

## What I will pay attention to

- **Speed:** How long does a task take, including checking and correction?
- **Quality:** What errors, omissions, or rework appear?
- **Learning:** Can I explain and reproduce the solution independently later?
- **Judgment:** Can I recognize when an answer is wrong or inappropriate?
- **Independence:** What happens when the tool is unavailable?

## What this can and cannot tell me

A personal field note is not a controlled experiment. Experience, task difficulty, and changing responsibilities can also affect performance. The aim is to document observations honestly, not to claim that one person's experience settles the broader debate.
